name: Memory (CLAUDE.md)
summary: Give Claude standing instructions about you and your project that it reads at the start of every session.
what: CLAUDE.md is a plain Markdown file of notes for Claude: build commands, code style, project conventions. Claude Code loads it when a session starts, so you don't repeat yourself each time. Files can live in your home folder (for all projects), in the project (shared with the team) or in a personal CLAUDE.local.md. Claude can also keep its own notes, called auto memory, in a folder per repository.

impact.title: No more repeating yourself
impact.detail: Commands, naming rules and gotchas written once are known in every new session.

impact.title: Shared team knowledge
impact.detail: A project CLAUDE.md committed to the repository gives everyone's sessions the same context.

impact.title: Personal and project layers
impact.detail: Your own preferences in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md sit alongside the project's file instead of replacing it.

howItWorks: Run /init in a project to have Claude write a starter CLAUDE.md, then edit it.
Put instructions for all your projects in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and project ones in ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md.
At launch, Claude Code loads the files from the working folder and every folder above it and combines them; files in subfolders load when Claude works there.
Pull in other files with @path/to/file lines, and open the files for editing with /memory.
Keep each file short: Claude treats it as guidance, so use permission rules or hooks for anything that must always be enforced.

events.note: Already part of Claude Code when the changelog began with this version.
CLAUDE.md files can import other files with @path lines.
